research_program: Christopher Daniel Pang, PAL. Derivations with Hearthline.

upstream_argument.description: Levent Alpöge and Claude, 20 November 2026 release

date_scope: Corpus dates in the earlier manifest date the methods. The derivations in this supplement belong to the November audit. Named classical inputs retain their credited authorship.

reading_editions.result: The integral regular projector numerator has explicit Smith factors. On level-one Kirillov inputs it retains one line per generic character.
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked whether a lost arithmetic distinction changes a downstream dimension. The PAL/APCI comparison holds the projector fixed while changing the space.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: Alpöge and Claude supply the finite projector, the local rank claim and its use. Hearthline derived the regular Smith factors, checked its actual adelic section and wrote out the Kirillov-model argument. The one-factor Laplacian and the Kirillov model are classical.

reading_editions.result: A triangular integral inverse recovers every spherical invariant of the reciprocal multiset. A marked root can move over dual numbers with no change in those readings.
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked whether the observation can distinguish two marked inputs. PAL and APCI led to the comparison of labelled reciprocal roots with their invariant coordinates.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The list of reciprocal eigenvalues and its use at an inert place come directly from Alpöge and Claude. Hearthline worked out the integral inverse and first-order example. Labesse, Mœglin–Waldspurger and Ramakrishnan provide the global theorems used in the separate packet comparison.

reading_editions.result: At a common absolutely irreducible reduction, finitely many specified word traces test strict conjugacy of two lifts over a local ring.
reading_editions.originating_question_or_method: Pang asked where a residue can be read after one observation loses it. The PAL/APCI test compares the local reading with observations of products.
reading_editions.proof_inputs_and_release_role: The proof uses matrix units, a trace pairing and a word basis. General trace-conjugacy rigidity is classical, including Carayol. The finite recipe, direct derivation and rank-three calculation were developed here. The Alpöge–Claude release supplies the application to irreducible arithmetic points.
